# MM-P1-L3-CN03-S1 Lubrication and fluids - Machining CNC turning center #3

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-CN03

Related documents: SB-1014, SOP-P1-L3-02, SOP-P1-L3-04

Scope
- This manual covers lubrication and fluid handling for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) located on line P1-L3. It defines required lubricants, refill triggers, approved procedures for filling and verification, and recordkeeping expectations. Refer to SB-1014 for safety barriers and to SOP-P1-L3-02 and SOP-P1-L3-04 for lockout and local work area procedures during servicing.

Background and rationale
- Proper lubrication is critical to preserve spindle accuracy, guideway life, feed drive performance, and to prevent premature component wear. The guidelines in this document are engineered to align maintenance effort with machine duty cycles and to minimize downtime risk while maintaining machining precision. Service technicians are expected to follow the procedures to ensure consistent application, avoid contamination, and provide auditable maintenance records.

Critical values (do not alter)
- The way lube refill interval for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) is 60 hours.  
- The lubricant part number for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) is CFW-LUB-662.

Tools and materials
- Manufacturer approved lubricant: CFW-LUB-662. Use only the specified part.  
- Clean dispensing funnel with integrated breather.  
- Portable pump rated for approved lubricant compatibility.  
- Lint-free wipes and approved solvent for cleaning fill caps and ports.  
- Static-resistant gloves and eye protection as required by SB-1014.  
- Machine-specific fill cup or adapter as described in SOP-P1-L3-02.  
- Maintenance log form and replacement tag stock for indicating next service.

Procedure
Preparation
- Review machine status and production schedule to select a planned opportunity for servicing that minimizes impact on operations. Consult SOP-P1-L3-04 for required isolation and lockout steps before accessing lubrication ports. Ensure a clean work area and that no coolant splash or swarf is present around fill points.

Verification
- Confirm current lubricant type in machine documentation and visual inspection by verifying labeling at the fill reservoir. Do not introduce any lubricant other than CFW-LUB-662. If label mismatch or contamination is suspected, escalate per SOP-P1-L3-02.

Access and cleaning
- Isolate the machine following SOP-P1-L3-04. Remove the fill cap and clean the immediate area with lint-free wipes and approved solvent. Avoid introducing airborne dust into open ports. Hold the cap over a clean surface to prevent contamination.

Refill sequence
- Top up the way lube reservoir using the clean dispensing funnel and portable pump until the reservoir reaches the fill indicator as designed by the equipment manufacturer. If the reservoir design does not provide a visible indicator, follow the visual and tactile cues described in the equipment maintenance drawing. Ensure no overfill; excess oil should be removed and returned to a sealed container labeled for disposal or return to stores according to site waste handling procedures.

Post-fill checks
- Replace the fill cap and secure all fittings. Run the machine through a controlled lubrication cycle as recommended by the equipment control panel to distribute lube to guideways. Observe for drip, leak, or unusual sound during the cycle. If leakage is observed, secure machine, clean the area, and remediate per SOP-P1-L3-02 before returning to service.

Examples and contextual guidance
- Example scenario: During a production shift change, the operator notes reduced slide motion smoothness. Maintenance reviews the machine log, confirms that the scheduled lubrication point is approaching the refill marker, and performs the refill using CFW-LUB-662 following the steps above. After servicing, feel test and a brief lubrication cycle confirm restoration of smooth motion and the machine returns to production without further adjustment.

Contamination control and handling
- Never mix lubricants. If contamination is suspected, drain the suspect lubricant into an approved container and tag it. Notify the maintenance planner and follow the contamination response in SB-1014. Clean reservoirs and ancillary piping prior to introducing a new batch of CFW-LUB-662.

Records and traceability
- For each service event, complete the maintenance log form. Record technician name, equipment id EQ-P1-L3-CN03, lubricant part number used CFW-LUB-662, the service action performed, and the reason for service. If servicing performed as part of scheduled activity tied to the way lube refill interval, reference the interval in the log entry. Attach any deviation or defect notes and reference SB-1014 and SOP-P1-L3-02 where applicable. Maintain records in the equipment file for audit and trending.

Acceptance criteria
- After completion of the procedure, acceptance is achieved when:
  - The reservoir contains the approved lubricant CFW-LUB-662 and is free from visible contamination.  
  - Machine lubricant distribution cycle runs without leakage or abnormal noise.  
  - Maintenance log for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 is completed with lubricant part number recorded and the action described.  
  - Any deviations have been recorded and corrective actions initiated in accordance with SB-1014 and SOP-P1-L3-02.

Notes on scheduling and monitoring
- Use the way lube refill interval for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) is 60 hours as the planning datum for preventive service scheduling. For high-use circumstances or abnormal wear indicators, increase inspection frequency and document rationale in the maintenance log.

Disposition and waste
- Dispose of used wipes, contaminated lubricant, and empty lubricant containers per site environmental procedures and SB-1014. Label containers and maintain disposal receipts in the equipment maintenance folder.

Revision control and references
- This document is controlled as Revision Rev D. For safety and lockout procedures consult SB-1014, SOP-P1-L3-02, and SOP-P1-L3-04. Any requests for change to procedures or to the specified lubricant must be submitted through the controlled document change process and reference the related documents listed above.
